pr.title: Print a Windows home path with a tilde (windows-portability.md §7.2)
pr.head: fa16bea59a44987e6710d47deb90107691f1ac9a

summary: field export builds labels and copies the results to ~/Desktop, or to the folder --to names, and prints one line per file saying where it landed. To keep that line short, it prints a path under your home folder with ~ in place of the home folder, through homeRelative in src/commands/export.ts.

On Windows that shortening never happened. homeRelative checked for the home path followed by /, but Windows paths use \, so every export printed its full C:\Users\… path. The Windows portability plan recorded this in its list of standalone defects (windows-portability.md §7.2).

This pull request gives homeRelative a separator parameter that defaults to path.sep, the platform's separator. A Windows path under the profile now prints as ~\Desktop\…, and because Windows paths ignore case, c:\users\me\Music prints as ~\Music too. A sibling folder such as C:\Users\justinx is still not treated as home, and macOS and Linux keep / and a case-sensitive comparison. The plan marks the item done.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The first head, ae05c15, also ported the sclang lookup. The author removed that in 6d640ad and left it to #186, so the two pull requests no longer overlap except in the plan file, where they edit different items.
  • The review of 6d640ad found that the existing homeRelative test failed on the Windows CI job, because its POSIX assertions took the Windows default separator there. fa16bea passes '/' in those assertions, and the thread is resolved.
  • fa16bea also took the review's suggestion to compare Windows paths without regard to case.

cards.title: Left for later
cards.html:
• On a OneDrive-redirected profile, the Desktop you see lives under OneDrive\Desktop, not where defaultExportDir() writes. The plan calls this a cosmetic wart, and it stays.
  • No Windows machine has run field export with this change. The unit test, which the Windows CI job also runs, is the only coverage.

groups.title: Shortening the home folder the way each platform compares paths
groups.kicker: How the export line decides whether a path is under your home folder
intro: homeRelative(path, home, separator) returns path with ~ in place of home when the path is the home folder itself or sits inside it. A path is inside the home folder only when it starts with the home path followed by a separator, so /Users/justinx never becomes ~x.

The change makes that separator a parameter. Its default is path.sep, which is / on macOS and Linux and \ on Windows, so the only caller, the export line in src/cli.ts, gets the right rule on each platform without passing anything. With \ as the separator, the home prefix also compares without regard to case, because Windows treats C:\Users and c:\users as the same folder. The part after the prefix prints exactly as given.

checks.text: The function compares only the first home.length characters of the path and slices the rest at that same index. So a character whose lowercase form is longer than its original cannot shift where the printed rest begins.

files.note: Adds the separator parameter, defaulting to path.sep, and splits the check into a prefix comparison, case-insensitive for \, and a test that the rest is empty or starts with the separator.

checks.text: On macOS, mocking node:path's sep to \ made homeRelative shorten c:\users\justin\Desktop\x.wav under the home C:\Users\justin to ~\Desktop\x.wav with the default separator, as a Windows host would.

files.note: Passes the separator explicitly in every assertion, so the test means the same on every host, and adds cases for Windows paths and for case: POSIX keeps it, Windows ignores it.

checks.text: This whole homeRelative block passes on macOS with node:path's sep mocked to \, as a Windows host sees it. With the lowercasing removed from homeRelative, only this assertion fails, so it pins the Windows rule.

groups.title: The plan records the item as done
groups.kicker: The Windows portability plan's list of standalone defects
intro: windows-portability.md §7.2 lists defects that the Windows sweep found outside any planned chunk. Each item stays in the list as a record, and a fixed one gains a dated Done note. This pull request adds that note to the homeRelative item and leaves the plan's status at in-progress.

files.note: Marks the homeRelative item done and says that the OneDrive Desktop stays a wart. The note describes the separator, not the case-insensitive comparison.
